title: Saying an unladylike thing
html_source: Rude Cissy dared to use a euphemism for “bottom” which is shocking to demure Gerty in this satire of Victorian propriety. Joyce is well aware that Ulysses will be considered shockingly obscene by readers using similar standards.

anchor.prefix:
ive him something, she said, so I would, where I won't say. 

 — On the beeoteetom, laughed Cissy merrily. 

 Gerty MacDowell bent down her head and crimsoned at the idea of Cissy
anchor.suffix: like that out loud she'd be ashamed of her life to say, flushing a deep rosy red, and Edy Boardman said she was sure the gentleman opposite heard what she said. But not a pin care
